claim: With the rat population growing in Washington, D.C., a group of residents is working to educate their neighbors about ways to prevent infestations without using rodenticides, according to an NPR story that caught Executive Editor Will Doig’s attention.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: NPR (via WUNC), 28 Sep 2026: 'rat numbers in Washington, D.C. are on the rise'; the D.C. Rat Rangers lead night walks teaching residents to prevent infestations with 'behavioral solutions that do not use rodenticides'. Will Doig's attention is not checked.
